markers.reading: The party stands on the road at the mountain edge in midmorning; the later clock answer places departure at about 10:00.

evidence.quote: It's midmorning, the centaurs having left shortly ago

time.basis: Opening narration, specified by the DM before departure.

markers.reading: Walking toward the stream takes about half an hour, ending at the unusual volcanic boulder.

evidence.quote: Takes you you know, a little not very long, maybe half an hour, to sort of walk towards the stream.

markers.reading: During the boulder investigation the DM identifies the current year as 211 after the Great War.

evidence.quote: The year 211 after the Great War.

markers.note: The transcript provides no conversion of this relative era into the YAML year 1748; no absolute year is inferred from it.

markers.reading: The party enters the gorge under the noonday sun; April is later confirmed during the discussion about leaving the horses.

evidence.quote: It's actually quite cool and peaceful as the heat of the of the now noonday sun fades away
It's—it's like April, so just past the equinox.

time.basis: Noonday narration, confirmed at the tunnel; month spoken later. Year/day remain YAML-only.

markers.reading: Delwath swims to the metal barrier in about 30 seconds and spends about 10 seconds inspecting it.

evidence.quote: takes you about 30 seconds, and you spend you know, 10 seconds or so looking around.

duration.basis: Approximately 30 seconds swimming plus 10 seconds looking, as narrated.

markers.note: The later return is established but not timed; the earlier 15-second return estimate is not independently confirmed.

markers.reading: Riswynn works the submerged chain for about two minutes before the plate slides down and the tunnel drains.

evidence.quote: and it's been two minutes, and the metal plate just slides into the floor

duration.basis: DM states elapsed time during the completed attempt.

markers.reading: The party climbs the corkscrew tunnel for approximately 30–40 minutes before reaching the upper chamber.

evidence.quote: probably 30, 40 minutes of kind of going up.

duration.basis: DM estimates elapsed climbing time, not the whole underground journey.

markers.reading: The search for a mechanism in the guard chamber has occupied a long, unspecified interval.

evidence.quote: You spent a long time searching and did not find any mechanism to open the door.

duration.basis: Retrospective statement of time actually spent searching; no numerical duration given.

markers.note: The later “40 minutes later” at u1261 accompanies a geology joke and is not a reliable measurement of this search.

markers.reading: Wellby finds the knob in the blank wall after about one minute of searching.

evidence.quote: It takes you—it takes Wellby only about a minute to find a small indentation to the wall to the left that has a little little stone knob that you can wiggle.

markers.reading: After the individual combat turns, the party spends roughly another minute wearing down the creature from outside its reach.

evidence.quote: So over the next minute or so, you just slowly wear it down

duration.basis: Explicit compressed resolution after the recorded initiative cycles.

yamlCheck.dateAnchor: April is spoken (t04); April 12 and the absolute year 1748 come from YAML. The spoken 211 after the Great War (t03) is not converted to DR by this transcript.
yamlCheck.explanation: Continuous same-day exploration and combat support no date transition. The YAML span is compatible, but its exact date and the conversion of the spoken relative year are not independently established; unmeasured conversation/search time does not justify an exact closing clock.
